# LLMs 101

> A free interactive mind map, plain-English guide, model directory, monthly tracker, and trends hub for large language models. Designed for anyone — technical or not — who wants to understand modern AI.

## Core pages

- [Mind Map](https://llms101.com/): Interactive mind map covering mathematics, training, model architectures, and prompting techniques. Click any node to expand deeper explanations with citations to primary research papers.
- [Full Guide](https://llms101.com/guide): Every mind map topic rendered as crawlable plain HTML — 27 topics across 5 sections including linear algebra, self-attention, RLHF, DPO, MoE architectures, RAG, and AI safety.
- [Model Directory](https://llms101.com/models): Superpower and trade-off profiles for every major frontier AI model family — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, DeepSeek, Mistral. Plain English, no benchmarks.
- [Model Tracker](https://llms101.com/tracker): Monthly updated human preference rankings and cost tier guide for frontier models. Based on Chatbot Arena Elo data with plain-English interpretation.
- [Trends](https://llms101.com/trends): Short plain-English explainers on the biggest shifts in AI — agentic workflows, cost collapse, reasoning models, open source developments. Published twice monthly.
- [State of LLMs Q2 2026](https://llms101.com/trends/state-of-llms-q2-2026): Flagship quarterly report covering model landscape, top trends, and what non-technical professionals need to know.
- [AI for Beginners](https://llms101.com/): Plain-English explanations of foundational AI concepts — what AI is, what LLMs are, how ChatGPT works, what tokens and hallucinations mean.
- [Learning Resources](https://llms101.com/): Curated list of the best free courses, papers, and tools for learning about LLMs.

## Key topics covered

- What is a Large Language Model (LLM)
- Transformer architecture and the attention mechanism
- Tokenisation and context windows
- Pre-training, fine-tuning, RLHF, DPO, and synthetic data
- Model families: GPT, Claude, Gemini, LLaMA, Mistral, DeepSeek, Qwen
- Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture
- Reasoning models: OpenAI o1/o3, DeepSeek R1
- Prompt engineering: zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, RAG
- Agentic AI workflows
- AI cost collapse and pricing trends
- Open vs closed weight models
- AI hallucination, bias, and safety
- Running AI locally with Ollama

## Quarterly reports

- Q2 2026: https://llms101.com/trends/state-of-llms-q2-2026
- Q1 2026: https://llms101.com/trends/state-of-llms-q1-2026
- Q4 2025: https://llms101.com/trends/state-of-llms-q4-2025

## Primary sources cited

- Vaswani et al. 2017 — "Attention Is All You Need": https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762
- Brown et al. 2020 — "Language Models are Few-Shot Learners" (GPT-3): https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165
- Ouyang et al. 2022 — "Training language models to follow instructions" (RLHF): https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155
- Rafailov et al. 2023 — "Direct Preference Optimization" (DPO): https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.18290
- Jiang et al. 2024 — "Mixtral of Experts": https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.04088
- DeepSeek 2025 — "DeepSeek-R1": https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
